text:
Maya (CEO): quick thread for folks who couldn't make the all-hands — recording is up, but dropping Q&A here about the customer win/loss patterns we discussed
Sam P. (VP Product): thanks — one question from Sales: when we say 'won on latency' what concrete thresholds are we using vs competitors?
Liam (Head of Sales): customers are explicitly quoting <50ms tail latency as a decision factor in a few RFPs last quarter. we lost two deals where they said 'we can't risk worst-case spikes'
Anya (PM): that's helpful. roadmap note: we're prioritizing tail SLO work (adaptive batching + pre-warm pools) in Q3 — should that be communicated as a specific SLA to prospective customers?
Maya (CEO): yes, transparency helps sales. propose we publish a small 'typical latency profile' doc and a note about our Dedicated SLA for enterprise. not exact numbers for hosted until we finish biz-review.
Rohit (Solutions Eng): practical ask from demos — customers want a simple knob for 'cost vs latency' for model routing. can we add a config example? e.g.,
```
route_policy: { priority: latency, max_cost_multiplier: 1.2 }
```
Elena (Customer Success): we've also seen customers win when we offered private deployment + eval assistance. for churn prevention, they flagged 'eval help' as the key differentiator, not just infra
Liam (Head of Sales): note — two losses were price-sensitive startups; they liked our perf but chose cheaper quantized self-host setups. pricing elasticity is real at < $X/month range (DM me for specifics)
Maya (CEO): does that mean we need a distinct 'starter' tier for Dedicated or a better self-serve guide for private infra?
Sam P. (VP Product): quick experiment idea: 1) publish a cost-optimized config with guidance for small teams, 2) test a limited 'Starter Dedicated' commit with lower min capacity for 3 months. measure conversion and churn
Anya (PM): I'll draft a short one-pager for Sales + CS by next Wed. MVP will include: recommended batch sizes, cache hints, and a quantization recommendation table
Rohit (Solutions Eng): add one practical item: example prompt benchmarks and tokenization gotchas. customers keep hitting tokenization/encoding surprises at scale
Elena (Customer Success): also add a checklist for evaluation support: data sanitization, privacy checklist, suggested eval prompts. this is what beats 'do it yourself' options
Liam (Head of Sales): actionable from Sales: can Leadership confirm we'll surface 'evaluation hours' as a negotiable add-on on contracts? that's closed multiple deals last quarter
Maya (CEO): yes — confirm we can offer limited paid eval assistance as an add-on. we should set clear SLAs on scope though (e.g., 10 engineering hours, one triage call). Sam, align with Legal on wording
Sam P. (VP Product): noted. I'll sync with Legal and Partner Ops. also will coordinate a short public note on latency expectations for Hosted vs Dedicated
Anya (PM): action items I captured: publish latency profile doc; create Starter Dedicated experiment; produce Sales/CS one-pager; draft eval-addendum for contracts. will send a follow-up thread with owners and ETA
DeployBot: _deployment_ completed: docs/stability/tail-slo-draft.md created by Anya at 2167890155 :white_check_mark:
Maya (CEO): love that momentum. last question from folks joining late: are we changing the roadmap priorities because of these wins/losses?
Sam P. (VP Product): minor reshuffle — tail SLOs and evaluation experience bumped up one sprint each. no change to major platform features timetable.
Liam (Head of Sales): cool — we'll route upcoming RFPs to Solutions Eng earlier in the cycle so we can offer eval scoping up-front
Elena (Customer Success): thanks — I'll update churn playbook to emphasize eval assistance as a retention lever
Maya (CEO): thanks everyone. if you have follow-ups, tag Anya or Sam. we'll review progress in the next leadership sync. :sparkles:
